title: The nearing tide, that rusty boot
html_source:
Stephen makes a statement about the visible world and the world is seeing. The change in syntax gives the impression of Stephen scanning the environment and arranging the world in a spectrum in front of him as colours are arranged by nature.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Was it only color as light wave he isolated or was it sound wave as well?… My thoughts lean towards meditation and a keen understanding that comes with the process of separating ones self from Dharma.

Joyce may have been venturing into the study of releasing ones self from a world of suffering through eastern practices of meditation.

artha, kama, dharma, moksha…. Sanskrit quoted by James Joyce, Finnegans Wake, 93.22 (1939)

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Spanish translate: Señales de todas las cosas que aquí estoy para leer, huevas y fucos de mar, el mar que enardece, aquella bota herrumbrosa (Subirat)

anchor.text: the nearing tide, that rusty boot
anchor.prefix:
[3]



Ineluctable modality of the visible: at least that if no more, thought through my eyes. Signatures of all things I am here to read, seaspawn and seawrack,
anchor.suffix: . Snotgreen, bluesilver, rust: coloured signs. Limits of the diaphane. But he adds: in bodies. Then he was aware of them bodies before of them coloured. How? By knocking his sconce
anchor.canonical_text: the nearing tide, that rusty boot
